newsitem.title: UK: UK farmers seek compensation for strong green pound.
newsitem.headline: UK farmers seek compensation for strong green pound.

text.p: Britain's National Farmers Union (NFU) is demanding that funds be made available to form a compensation package for farmers following the third revaluation of the green pound in the past six months.

"It is estimated that this (latest) revaluation of nearly three percent will contribute to a fall in the value of farm output in 1997 in excess of 1.5 billion sterling, as a result of the total revaluations over the past year," said NFU president Sir David Naish.
"This is clearly a massive blow to the industry," he said in an NFU press release.
"The latest revaluation has brought an added burden to farmers as arable area payments as well as market prices will be hit." he added.

Naish said that in other EU countries where green rate revaluations occurred, the governments have sought and been granted an EU compensation package as well as, in some cases, further funds from their National Treasurys.
"It is inconceivable that the British Government would allow our industry to be financially penalised compared with all our European competitors." Naish said.
He urged the British governement to act immediately to ensure the EU Commission released the necessary funds.
"The ball is now clearly in the court of the new (British) government to illustrate its support for the agricultural industry," he said.
